requirement:
An item with no attachments has an empty list. A language may return empty
lists for every item.
rationale:
The requirement has two obligations. An item with no attachments has an empty list. A language may return empty lists for every item. The second is a MAY, so it imposes nothing to check.

1. **Empty list for an item with no attachments.**
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` builds an `OutlineItem::new(...)` and asserts `item.attachments.is_empty()`. That shows the default for an item with no attachments is an empty list.
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` runs real bundled-language parsing. It flattens the attachments of all items and compares them exactly to the expected list. Any item without an expected attachment must therefore have an empty list, because any extra attachment would fail the equality. The `test.md` case includes non-comment HTML, an inline comment, a comment inside a code fence, and an unfinished comment. In each of these an item that should have no attachments is checked.
   - The `test.txt` case (`# just text`) expects `vec![]`. This exercises the case where a language returns no attachments for any item, and the assertion enforces it.

2. **Marking.** Both tests carry `{test}` references to `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.empty`.

I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the requirement.
